ce_bugs.text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:52 — Any attendee (including one just added by another attendee) can add more guests, giving unbounded recursive spam amplification from Cal.com's domain with no rate limit or array-size cap.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — Email send failure is swallowed with a console.log and the mutation still returns success, so the UI shows "Guests added" while nobody was notified.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:20 — No check that the booking is not CANCELLED, REJECTED, or in the past, so guests can be attached to and mailed about dead bookings.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:165 — Attendees are committed to the DB before updateCalendarAttendees; a throw there leaves guests persisted, calendar unsynced, and no emails sent while the client sees an error.

packages/emails/email-manager.ts:541 — New-guest detection uses the raw `guests` input rather than the actually-inserted uniqueGuests, so an existing attendee resubmitted in the input gets a fresh "scheduled" email and blacklisted/dropped addresses are mis-classified.

packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts:27 — Subject uses calEvent.attendees[0].name unguarded and replyTo lists every attendee email, exposing the full attendee list to the organizer's mail client and crashing if attendees is empty.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — guests array lacks .min(1), max length, and uniqueness/lowercase normalization, so the server accepts empty/duplicate/case-variant emails the client-side schema rejects.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:169 — sendAddGuestsEmails is passed the raw `guests` input rather than the filtered `uniqueGuests`, so already-existing/blacklisted attendees can be misclassified as new and re-sent a full invite.
packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts:27 — Subject uses this.calEvent.attendees[0].name unguarded; an empty attendees array throws at render time in this email contract.
packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:77 — Blacklist entries are lowercased but the guest email is not, so mixed-case addresses bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS.
packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts:28 — this.calEvent.attendees[0].name` throws when the attendee list is empty, breaking organizer email send.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:58 — booking.userId || 0` sentinel makes findFirstOrThrow surface a raw Prisma 500 for bookings with a null userId instead of a typed TRPC error.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:165 — eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` is unguarded, so a calendar-sync failure rejects the mutation after attendees were already persisted, leaving inconsistent state.
apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:49 — Empty guest list returns silently with no user feedback, and `isInvalidEmail` is never reset when the user edits the emails.
packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — Server schema accepts an empty `guests` array and does not enforce uniqueness, relying solely on client-side validation.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — Emails are sent with the raw `guests` input instead of the computed `uniqueGuests`, making the dedupe/blacklist filtering partly dead for the email path.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:81 — Blacklist emails are lowercased but incoming guest emails and existing attendee emails are compared case-sensitively, an inconsistency that will drift.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:165 — eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees is not wrapped in try/catch, so a calendar/video provider failure throws after attendees are already committed to the DB, leaving booking and calendar out of sync with no rollback or retry.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:169 — Email send failure is swallowed with a bare console.log that drops the error object, so guests are silently never notified and the failure is undiagnosable.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92 — The attendee DB write, calendar update, and email send are three unguarded sequential steps with no transaction or compensating action, so any mid-sequence failure leaves a permanent partial state.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:107 — Blacklist comparison lowercases the configured list but not the submitted guest email, so blacklisted addresses submitted with different casing bypass the filter.
packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts:26 — Subject line dereferences this.calEvent.attendees[0].name without a guard, throwing during send if the attendee list is empty.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:52 — Any attendee (including a guest previously added by an attacker) passes the permission check and can add further guests, unlike sibling handlers that gate on organizer/team-admin.
packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:77 — Blacklist entries are lowercased but the submitted guest email is not, so `Foo@Bar.com` bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — Newly added arbitrary emails receive a full scheduled-event email/ICS including video call URL, meeting id and meeting password, leaking booking secrets to attacker-chosen addresses.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — guests array has no max length or rate limiting, allowing a single authenticated request to trigger unbounded outbound emails (mail-bomb / reputation abuse).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158 — EventManager is built from the requesting user's credentials rather than the booking organizer's, letting a non-organizer drive calendar mutations under mismatched identity.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:167 — sendAddGuestsEmails is called with raw `guests` rather than `uniqueGuests`, and no test pins the recipient set.
